capabilities: fetch artifacts from GitLab Generic Package Registry or GitHub Releases
unzip downloads and mirror contents into a chosen vault folder
refresh sources on intervals, on focus, or at startup with freshness checks
store access tokens in the OS keychain via app.secretStorage
share fetched content across devices directly or through Halyard Sync
disambiguation: Not a git sync tool; it only downloads and mirrors remote artifacts read-only, with no clone, push, or write path back to the source.
extras: The README states the plugin was developed with substantial AI assistance (Claude). It is not yet in the community plugin directory; installation is via BRAT or manual download. CI-artifact and plain-URL sources are designed for but not built.
motivation: The author built it because read-only artifact ingestion sits outside obsidian-git's scope.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to pull generated artifacts from a remote registry into a vault folder on a schedule without git.

relations.evidence: the plugin that defined git-in-Obsidian. Halyard Fetch exists because read-only artifact ingestion sits outside its scope
For the git-based sibling, see Halyard Sync, which syncs a whole vault with a git repository
zip handling, pure JS with no native dependency, which is what makes mobile support possible

summary: Scheduled fetcher that downloads GitLab package or GitHub release artifacts, unzips them, and mirrors the contents into a vault folder.
